standard_prerequisites.name: Sign and triviality criteria for invertible sheaves on a proper curve
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a nonzero section on a component of nonpositive degree into a nowhere-vanishing one.

core_obligations: For a nonzero section s of L, use reducedness to find an irreducible component C with s|_C nonzero (proof lines 9986-9987).

Apply the degree criterion to conclude that s is nowhere vanishing on C, because a nonzero section of an invertible sheaf of degree at most zero on a proper curve is nowhere vanishing (proof lines 9988-9990).
Propagate: s is nowhere vanishing on every component meeting C, and connectedness forces this to hold on all components, so s vanishes nowhere and L is trivial (proof lines 9991-9994).
proof_roadmap: Find a component where the section is nonzero.
Use the curve criterion to make it nowhere vanishing there.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an invertible sheaf L on a proper, reduced, connected, equidimensional scheme of dimension one whose restriction to every irreducible component has nonpositive degree, either H^0(X, L) vanishes or L is trivial. The proof takes a nonzero section s, uses reducedness to find a component C on which s restricts nontrivially, and invokes the degree criterion on curves to conclude that s is nowhere vanishing on C (proof lines 9986-9990). It then propagates nowhere-vanishing to every component meeting C and uses connectedness to conclude that s vanishes nowhere, whence L is trivial (proof lines 9991-9994). H2: the propagation of nowhere-vanishing across the components using connectedness is the substance.
